newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares pare gains but still end higher.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares pare gains but still end higher.

text.p: Brazilian stocks pared some early gains but still closed higher in healthy trade, boosted by benchmark Telebras and early gains in Wall Street prices, brokers said.
"The market opened way up then fluctuated during the day on profit-taking," a local broker said.
The Sao Paulo bourse's Bovespa .BVSP index of 48 most-traded shares ended up 0.70 percent at 10,715 points in hefty trade of 791.3 million reais ($746.5 million).
Brokers said the bolsa opened with a wave of buying, particularly in bellwether Telebras after Tuesday's night's lower house panel approval of a bill regulating Brazil's telecoms sector.
It also was heartened by news that BNDESPar, the investment arm of Brazil's National Development Bank, will sell a tiny stake in state oil firm Petrobras Friday.

Petrobras' common surged 4.65 percent to 199.90 reais while its preferred dropped 2.96 percent to 245.50 reais as both issues adjusted to the base price of 225.80 reais the government has set on the 550 million preferred shares it plans to sell.
Telebras' preferred rose as high as 137.50 reais before falling back to close at 135.90 reais, for a gain on the day of 0.89 percent. Its common ended up 1.02 percent at 128.30 reais.
Brokers also said a strong rises on Wall Street also aided the day's rise in the Bovespa. "The market remained pegged to the Dow," a trader said.
The market closed amid profit-taking and some caution ahead of a Senate vote on a bill allowing President Fernando Henrique Cardoso to stand for re-election next year.

Investors also expressed some concern regarding the slow pace of civil service reforms that have been stalled in Congress and are keeping an eye on possible political fallout from a cash-for-votes scandal that erupted last week.
Among other blue chips, recently privatized miner Cia Vale do Rio Doce closed up a healthy 1.22 percent at 24.80 reais.

Despite rises in key power stocks, the bolsa's Electrical Energy Index .IEE slipped 0.42 percent to end at 2,767 points led by a 3.75 percent plunge in preferred shares of state-owned Companhia Paulista de Forca e Luz (CPFL) to 156.39 reais.

Eletrobras' preferred B rose 0.78 percent to 514.00 reais but Minas Gerais state's Cemig soared 3.5 percent on news the government plans to sell its 32.9 percent stake next week and Sao Paulo state's Cesp preferred jumped 2.86 percent.
